_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard (041), Series WX1YZ/5, SET-1. 27 page images (cover says 27 printed pages): idx 0 bilingual cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions + Hindi Q1-3; English on every even index 2-26, Hindi on every odd index 3-25 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet, all Hindi (idx 17 and idx 25 confirmed at full size: Hindi Q33(b)/34/35 and Hindi Q38(iii)); idx 26 is the last page and is English. General Instructions (i)-(x) confirm full80: 38 questions, A Q1-18 MCQ + Q19-20 A-R @1, B Q21-25 @2, C Q26-31 @3, D Q32-35 @5, E Q36-38 case studies @4. Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 in E: Q21, Q25, Q26, Q28, Q33, Q34, Q36, Q37, Q38, all found on the paper, and the marking-scheme walk shows a bare OR for exactly these nine (Q32's scheme carries an alternative SOLUTION for a second figure, not an alternative question). Section-A keys read off the marking scheme for 30/5/1 as images and each re-derived: all agree; no void notes anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points are RAISED dots on this paper (Q4, Q8, Q10, Q17, Q35, Q36). Section E prints 'Case Study - N' headings, kept in _caseStudyLabel only. Q38 (ii) is a four-choice item whose choices are graphs; kept as a subjective case-study row (see its _flag). Opener of series 30/5: nothing skipped.

questions.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions carrying 1 mark each. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** If the points \(A(4, 3)\) and \(B(x, 5)\) lie on a circle with centre \(O(2, 3)\), then the value of x is 2.

**Reason (R) :** Centre of a circle is the mid-point of each chord of the circle.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

Which of the following types of graph represents \(p(t)\) ?

(a) Graph (a) as printed - a downward-opening curve starting at O that rises and comes back to the time axis at 5/4; see the attached figure.

(b) Graph (b) as printed - a downward-opening curve starting at O whose highest point is above 5/4 (dashed line), meeting the time axis beyond 5/4; see the attached figure.

(c) Graph (c) as printed - an upward-opening curve through O and 5/4 that dips below the time axis between them; see the attached figure.

(d) Graph (d) as printed - a downward-opening curve that starts below the time axis and touches it at 5/4; see the attached figure.
